text: A 6-month-old boy is brought to the OPD due to poor feeding. His mother says that he has difficulty holding his head up while breastfeeding and his suckling seems weaker than usual. Weight is at the 5th percentile. Length and head circumference are tracking along the 25th percentile. Physical examination shows hepatomegaly and hypotonia in all 4 limbs. Cardiac auscultation shows a gallop rhythm, and chest x-ray reveals severe cardiomegaly. Muscle biopsy shows enlarged lysosomes containing periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)–positive material. Which of the following enzymes is most likely deficient in this patient?

A 33-year-old man comes to the OPD due to several months of episodic headaches accompanied by sweating and feelings of anxiety that spontaneously resolve after 15-30 minutes. CT scan of the abdomen reveals a mass in the right adrenal gland. Which of the following cells have the same embryologic origin as the tissue responsible for this patient's current condition?

A 58-year-old man, working in a software company, with a history of smoking and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) presents to the emergency department with a 5-day history of fever, cough, shortness of breath, and diarrhea. One of his colleagues was admitted to the hospital the previous week. On examination, he has a temperature of 102.2°F, a heart rate of 110 beats per minute, and crackles on auscultation of the right lower lung field. Blood tests reveal low sodium. Given this patient’s presentation, what is the investigation of choice to confirm the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her neighbors 30 minutes after they found her unconscious in her yard. Her neighbors report that she has been spending more time at home by herself because she recently lost her job. On arrival, she is unable to provide a history. Her pulse is 76/min, respirations are 13/min, and blood pressure is 114/72 mm Hg. Examination shows significant weakness of the left upper and lower extremities. She is unable to plantarflex the ankle while supine. She is able to stand on her toes. Her gait is unsteady. Deep tendon reflexes are 3+ and symmetric. A CT scan of the head shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old college student presents with a 2-week history of low-grade fever, fatigue, and a non-productive cough. A chest X-ray shows diffuse peribronchial infiltrates with thickened bronchial markings, but no lobar consolidation. The patient reports no significant improvement with amoxicillin started by his primary care physician a week ago. Which of the following best explains why this organism is resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics?

options.label: B
options.text: Reduced permeability of the bacterial membrane to antibiotics

options.label: C
options.text: Lack of a peptidoglycan-containing cell wall

options.label: D
options.text: Efflux pumps that actively expel antibiotics

text: A 41-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a suicide attempt. His wife found him on the bathroom floor with an empty bottle of medication next to him. He has a history of major depressive disorder. His only medication is nortriptyline. Examination shows dilated pupils and dry skin. An ECG shows tachycardia and a QRS complex width of 130 ms. In addition to intravenous fluid resuscitation, which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?

A 36-year-old man with HIV presents with a two-week history of malaise and non-productive cough. A chest X-ray reveals bilateral patchy interstitial infiltrates. He is started on high-dose intravenous trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) for presumed Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP). The patient should be specifically monitored for which of the following?
A 50-year-old man suddenly developed right-sided weakness and aphasia within 2 hours. His BP recorded was 160/110 mmHg and NCCT was clear. What is the next step in management?

options.label: A
options.text: CT angiography to look for large vessel occlusion

options.label: B
options.text: MRI to look for infarct Occlusion

text: A group of investigators is studying the association between a fire retardant chemical used on furniture and interstitial lung disease. They use hospital records to identify 50 people who have been diagnosed with interstitial lung disease. They also identify a group of 50 people without interstitial lung disease who are matched in age and geographic location to those with the disease. The participants' exposure to the chemical is assessed by surveys and home visits. Which of the following best describes this study design?

A 21-year-old man, after a bout of binge drinking and vomiting, presents with severe pain in the chest and dyspnea with a crunch on palpation in the back. On clinical examination, there is rigidity in the upper abdomen. The chest X-ray shows a Naclerio V sign. Which of the following statements is false about this condition?

options.label: A
options.text: Cervical esophagostomy is performed in unstable patients

options.label: B
options.text: Perforation is most commonly seen on the left anterolateral wall

options.label: C
options.text: ﻿﻿﻿Gingko leaf sign may be seen on CXR

text: A 64-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease undergoes coronary artery bypass surgery. His postoperative course is complicated by hypotension, which is treated successfully with intravenous fluids; however, a few hours later, he experiences severe abdominal pain followed by bloody diarrhea. Abdominal examination shows normal bowel sounds, with no significant guarding or focal tenderness. The venous lactic acid level is elevated. An abdominal CT scan is ordered which shows edema at the anastomotic bridging between the right and left terminal branches of the ascending left colic artery. What is this point referred to as?

A 27-year-old woman presents with a thyroid nodule. Serum TSH is normal. Ultrasound of her thyroid reveals a 1.5-cm hypoechoic nodule in the right thyroid lobe with irregular margins, internal microcalcifications, and internal vascularity. FNAC is performed which is reported as Thy3 Bethesda grade. Which of the following is the next most appropriate step in management of this patient?
Which imaging modality is the investigation of choice to diagnose dysphagia lusoria?

A 28-year-old nulligravid woman comes to the physician for infertility and dyspareunia workup. She also reports episodic back and pelvic pain over the past 6 months that lasts for 2-3 days; she has missed several days of work each month because of the pain. Menarche was at the age of 13 years, and menses occur at 26-28 day intervals. Pelvic examination shows a normal-appearing vulva and vagina. There is rectovaginal tenderness. Ultrasonography of the pelvis shows a retroverted normal-sized uterus. Further evaluation is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.label: A
options.text: Endometrial tissue within the myometrium on biopsy

options.label: B
options.text: Multiple bilateral ovarian cysts on ultrasonography

options.label: D
options.text: Concentric, solid myometrial tumors on MRI

text: Which of the following is the best investigation to detect myocardial perfusion?

A patient presented to the casualty with chest pain and palpitations. His blood pressure was 130/90 mmHg and pulse rate 101 bpm. Echocardiography showed a collapse of the right atrium during diastole. What is the most appropriate management for this patient?

A 60-year-old female with a history of hypertension presents with chest pain and dyspnea. The physician is concerned about a pulmonary embolism (PE) and orders two diagnostic tests: D-dimer test CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) The tests are ordered in parallel to confirm the diagnosis of PE. Which of the following is the most likely outcome of performing both tests together?

options.label: A
options.text: Increased likelihood of diagnosing PE in the early stage

options.label: C
options.text: Increased negative predictive value (NPV) for PE

text: In a patient with history of trauma of forearm and X-ray showing fracture of proximal part of medial bone with dislocation of proximal part of lateral bone. Which of the following muscles may be paralyzed?

Which of the following statements regarding chest trauma are true? ECG should be performed in all cases with associated sternal fracture Underwater seal drainage is indicated if pneumothorax is present Diaphragmatic rupture is best diagnosed by surgical exploration Urgent surgery is required in all cases of massive hemothorax Sternal fractures are markers of possible associated internal injuries

A young patient comes to the emergency with pain in the right leg after falling from a height. The radiological image shows a physeal injury fracture extending to epiphysis. What is the type of Salter-Harris physeal injury mentioned above?

A 48-year-old post-cholecystectomy patient presents with pain in the right upper quadrant on the third postoperative day. Evaluation reveals a collection in Morrison's pouch. A bile leak was suspected. Which of the following investigations will be most helpful in this case?

An ultrasound scan of a 35-year-old woman revealed a unilocular cyst of 5 cm in her ovary. She is asymptomatic. She does not have a family history of breast, ovarian, or colon cancer. She has not received treatment for infertility in the past. CA-125 levels are <35 U/mL. What is the next best step in her treatment plan?

A 63-year woman old presents to the AIIMS emergency chest pain after an RTA. Which resulted in crushed left lower limb. ECG shows 1-2 mm ST elevations in leads V2-V4 & troponin are elevated. The patient undergoes CAG which was normal. Which of the following is likely?

options.label: B
options.text: Apical hyperkinesis with free wall akinesia

options.label: C
options.text: Severe mitral regurgitation with papillary muscle dysfunction

text: A 66-year-old woman presents to the clinic with 2 months of worsening fatigue and persistent lower back pain that is aggravated by movement. Physical examination shows pallor and tenderness over the lower spine. Radiographic imaging reveals lytic bone lesions. Laboratory findings include: Hemoglobin: 8.5 g/dL Serum creatinine: 2.8 mg/dL Serum calcium: 11.0 mg/dL Urine dipstick is negative for protein, but 24-hour urine protein quantification shows elevated protein levels. Urine electrophoresis is most likely to detect which of the following?

An 82-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a syncopal episode. He has had no chest pain or dyspnea but he has constipation of recent onset. He was hospitalized 2 weeks ago for atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response and was discharged home with oral medications after appropriate management. Medical history is also significant for hypertension and severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease requiring home supplemental oxygen. ECG shows new-onset second-degree atrioventricular block. Which of the following drugs is the most likely cause of his current condition?

A 61-year-old woman with a history of unstable angina complains of hematemesis after retching and vomiting following a night of binge drinking. Which of the following is the next recommended step in the management of this patient?

options.label: C
options.text: Exploratory laparotomy, gastrotomy, and oversewing of the tear

text: A 65-year-old female with a history of heart failure and chemotherapy for breast cancer is evaluated using a MUGA scan to assess cardiac function. What specific aspect of heart function is primarily evaluated by a MUGA scan?

options.label: A
options.text: Coronary artery blood flow and ischemia.

options.label: B
options.text: Myocardial perfusion during exercise and rest.

options.label: C
options.text: Function of the ventricles, particularly the ejection fraction.

options.label: D
options.text: Evaluation of valvular function and regurgitation.

text: A 33-year-old man presents with a 2-day history of left knee pain and swelling. He has no prior joint pain, trauma, fever, rash, or systemic symptoms. His medical history includes seasonal allergies, and he takes loratadine as needed. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Examination reveals a moderate left knee effusion, slight warmth without erythema, and no ligamentous laxity or joint locking. Laboratory results show elevated ESR (46 mm/hr), normal blood counts, and creatinine. X-ray reveals linear calcifications of the menisci and articular cartilage, and synovial fluid analysis shows 15,400/mm³ leukocytes (80% neutrophils) with a negative Gram stain. Which of the following additional tests is most appropriate in the evaluation of this patient’s symptoms?

options.label: B
options.text: Antinuclear antibody and double-stranded DNA antibody assay

text: A 45-year-old male presents to the clinic complaining of fever, headache, and a persistent dry cough. He mentions that his symptoms started a few days after he was cleaning an old, abandoned aviary. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild respiratory distress. A chest X-ray is performed, revealing interstitial infiltrates. Laboratory investigations, including serology, indicate atypical pneumonia with inclusion bodies suggestive of a zoonotic infection. Based on these findings, the physician is considering the diagnosis of a specific zoonotic atypical pneumonia. Which inclusion body is most likely associated with this patient’s diagnosis?

A 60-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by ambulance for right-sided weakness and slurred speech that started 30 minutes ago. The wife reports that her husband said he was dizzy, and shortly after, he developed acute right arm and leg weakness and was unable to speak. Medical history includes hypertension, for which he takes amlodipine. The patient also takes an aspirin daily. Blood pressure is 225/110 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, and respirations are 20/min. On examination, the patient is alert but aphasic with 0/5 strength in the right upper and lower extremities. Examination of the left upper and lower extremities is normal. A nicardipine infusion is started and CT scan of the head is performed. After returning from the CT scanner, the patient is minimally responsive and has developed hyperextension of all four extremities. CT scan shows a left-sided intracerebral hemorrhage with a 5-mm midline shift to the right. Which of the following is the best next step in management of this patient?

A 60-year-old man comes to the office due to pain, redness, and swelling in his right arm. The patient was recently diagnosed with unresectable lung cancer. He received the first cycle of chemotherapy 2 weeks ago through a right-sided peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC). Temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), blood pressure is 130/80 mm Hg, pulse is 78/min, and respirations are 14/min. Oxygen saturation is normal. Examination shows right arm swelling and mild erythema. Capillary refill is normal. No discharge is seen around the PICC line. The remainder of the examination is normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 20-year-old, previously healthy woman is brought to the emergency department after a motor vehicle collision. On arrival at the emergency department, blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg and pulse is 120/min. On physical examination, the patient is alert but appears anxious, pale, and diaphoretic. Several actively bleeding lacerations are present on the lower extremities. X-rays show pelvic and left femoral shaft fractures. Which of the following findings are most likely present in this patient?

options.label: A
options.text: Cardiac contractility high, baroreceptor firing high, ANP high

options.label: B
options.text: Cardiac contractility low, baroreceptor firing high, ANP high

options.label: C
options.text: Cardiac contractility high, baroreceptor firing low, ANP low

options.label: D
options.text: Cardiac contractility low, baroreceptor firing high, ANP low

text: A 65-year-old woman comes to the emergency department due to a 5-day history of left lower abdominal pain, nausea, and poor appetite. Although she has a history of chronic constipation, she has been having 2–3 loose, non bloody bowel movements daily. Three years ago, the patient was admitted to the hospital for a similar episode. History is notable for hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy 15 years ago. Temperature is 38.8°C (101.8°F), blood pressure is 122/82 mm Hg, and pulse is 98/min. She appears to be in moderate discomfort due to pain and cannot find a comfortable resting position. Abdominal examination shows left lower quadrant tenderness and guarding but no rebound tenderness; there is a palpable, tender mass. Rectal and pelvic examinations elicit exquisite left-sided tenderness. Stool testing for occult blood is negative. Laboratory results include a white blood cell count of 16,500/mm³. Which of the following is the best next step in diagnosis?
Arrange the following in sequential order: MSAFP, E3, HCG, Inhibin-A TIFA scan Growth-Liquor scan NT-NB

A 35-year-old man comes to the clinic for evaluation of exertional dyspnea and dry cough for 8 months. Oxygen saturation on room air while lying down is 96% and drops to 88% after 6 minutes of walking. Examination shows fine crackles in both lower lungs. Chest x-ray reveals reticular densities in both lung fields. Lung biopsy shows an infiltration of inflammatory cells, predominantly lymphocytes, as well as poorly formed noncaseating granulomas and moderate alveolar septal fibrosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the subsequent options is non-essential in the evaluation of mosaic Turner syndrome?

A 65-year-old male presents with sepsis and purpura fulminans. Thromboelastography (TEG) is ordered to assess the patient's clotting profile. Which of the following TEG tracings is most consistent with the patient's presentation?

options.label: A
options.text: Reduced R-time, increased angle, increased MA, increased LY30

options.label: B
options.text: Prolonged R-time, decreased angle, decreased MA, decreased LY30

options.label: C
options.text: Prolonged R-time, increased angle, decreased MA, increased LY30

options.label: D
options.text: Reduced R-time, decreased angle, increased MA, decreased LY30

text: A previously healthy 51-year-old man is brought to the emergency department because of confusion for 2 hours. His wife reports that he fell and hit his head while changing a ceiling light the previous evening. On arrival, he is unconscious. His temperature is 37.1°C (98.8ºF), pulse is 54/min, respirations are 8/min and irregular, and blood pressure is 198/106 mm Hg. The right pupil is dilated and fixed; the left pupil is round and reactive to light. There is extension of the extremities to painful stimuli. He is intubated and mechanically ventilated. A mannitol infusion is begun. A noncontrast CT scan of the brain shows herniation of the right medial temporal lobe. Which of the following is the most likely additional finding in this patient?
Which of the following is the best method for detecting and localization of tumors associated with pheochromocytomas?
A 40-year-old male presents with poor urinary stream, hesitancy, and straining. He has a history of pelvic trauma a year ago. Which is the most appropriate initial investigation?

A 52-year-old woman with SLE on long-term steroids undergoes uneventful laparoscopic appendectomy. Postoperatively, she develops refractory hypotension. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
During a modified radical mastectomy, the pectoralis minor and level III lymph nodes are removed while preserving the pectoralis major. Which procedure was performed?

A 60-year-old diabetic male presents with severe right ear pain, discharge, and granulation tissue in the external auditory canal (EAC). He was treated for otitis externa two weeks ago, but his symptoms have worsened. The physician is concerned about the possibility of malignant otitis externa extending into the skull base. Which imaging modality is most appropriate to assess the extent of his infection?

options.label: A
options.text: CT scan of the temporal bone

options.label: B
options.text: MRI of the head and neck

text: A 70-year-old patient with poorly controlled diabetes presents with symptoms suggestive of malignant otitis externa. The physician considers further imaging to assess the extent of the disease. What is the primary role of a Technetium-99m scan in this clinical scenario?

options.label: B
options.text: To evaluate the extent of bone involvement

options.label: C
options.text: To assess the function of the Eustachian tube

options.label: D
options.text: To determine the presence of middle ear effusion

text: Which of the following statements regarding the diagnosis and workup of glomus tumors is false?

options.label: A
options.text: Preoperative biopsy is avoided due to high vascularity and risk of injury

options.label: B
options.text: CT scan using bone window helps identify caroticojugular spine erosion in glomus jugulare

options.label: C
options.text: Serum catecholamines and urinary VMA levels are checked in all patients

options.label: D
options.text: MRI is not useful in assessing the soft tissue extent or vascular invasion

text: A 45-year-old female presents with pulsatile tinnitus and conductive hearing loss. Otoscopy reveals a reddish mass behind the intact tympanic membrane that blanches on applying pressure with Siegel’s speculum. Which of the following is true regarding her likely diagnosis?

options.label: A
options.text: Biopsy is the investigation of choice to confirm glomus tympanicum

options.label: B
options.text: CT scan shows salt and pepper appearance due to tumor vascularity

options.label: C
options.text: Most glomus tumors are functional and secrete catecholamines

options.label: D
options.text: The tumor most likely arises from the promontory and receives blood from the ascending pharyngeal artery

text: Which of the following statements regarding Electronystagmography (ENG) is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: ENG is based on detecting auditory evoked potentials from the cochlea

options.label: B
options.text: ENG cannot detect nystagmus that is not visible to the naked eye

options.label: C
options.text: ENG uses corneoretinal potentials recorded via electrodes placed around the eyes

options.label: D
options.text: ENG is only useful for recording spontaneous nystagmus and not stimulus-induced types

text: Which of the following statements regarding posturography is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It is used to evaluate only the vestibular component of balance control

options.label: B
options.text: It relies on altering visual, vestibular, and somatosensory inputs to assess postural stability

options.label: C
options.text: It provides definitive diagnosis of vestibular disorders

options.label: D
options.text: Posturography must be performed with a moving platform only

text: Which of the following best describes the Submentovertical (SMV) view used in radiological imaging of the skull base?

options.label: A
options.text: X-ray beam is directed cephalocaudally with occiput on the film

options.label: B
options.text: It visualizes external auditory canal, middle ear cleft, sphenoid sinus, and carotid canal

options.label: C
options.text: It is primarily used to assess frontal and ethmoid sinuses

options.label: D
options.text: It fails to demonstrate foramina at the base of skull like foramen ovale and spinosum

text: A 10-year-old child presents with high-grade fever, neck rigidity, photophobia, vomiting, and altered sensorium. He had a history of ear discharge for the past few days. CSF analysis reveals turbid fluid, high protein, low glucose, and predominant polymorphs. Which of the following statements regarding this condition is most accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: It is most commonly associated with otitis externa in children

options.label: B
options.text: Lumbar puncture is contraindicated in all cases of suspected meningitis

options.label: C
options.text: CT scan is the definitive diagnostic test for bacterial meningitis

options.label: D
options.text: It is the most common intracranial complication of otitis media in children

text: A 55-year-old man with a history of smoking and alcohol use presents with dysphagia, weight loss, and a hoarse voice. A biopsy of a lesion in the supraglottis confirms squamous cell carcinoma. Laryngoscopic examination reveals a tumor involving the mucosa of the base of the tongue and the medial wall of the pyriform sinus without fixation of the larynx. A CT scan shows the presence of a single 4 cm lymph node metastasis in the ipsilateral neck. No distant metastasis is detected. What is the most appropriate TNM staging for this patient's carcinoma of the supraglottis?

A 65-year-old male patient with a history of smoking presents with a persistent sore throat and difficulty swallowing. On examination, he is found to have a tumor involving the mucosa of the base of the tongue and the medial wall of the pyriform sinus. The tumor does not cause fixation of the larynx. A CT scan shows the presence of a single ipsilateral lymph node metastasis measuring 4 cm in the neck. There is no evidence of distant metastasis. Based on the provided TNM staging system for carcinoma of the supraglottis, what is the appropriate staging for this patient?

A 32-year-old woman presents with a history of progressive difficulty breathing, particularly with exertion, and a high-pitched wheezing. She has a past medical history of prolonged intubation following a severe motor vehicle accident two years ago. A CT scan of the neck reveals a narrowed airway at the level of the cricoid cartilage. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old boy presents with fever, bilateral nasal obstruction, swelling over the bridge of the nose, and tenderness for 3 days. On anterior rhinoscopy, bilateral smooth septal swelling is noted with fluctuation. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.label: A
options.text: CT scan of paranasal sinuses to assess sinusitis

options.label: B
options.text: High-dose steroids to reduce mucosal inflammation

options.label: C
options.text: Incision and drainage with systemic antibiotics

text: Allergic rhinitis is differentiated from non-allergic rhinitis by:

options.label: D
options.text: CT PNS (Computed Tomography of the Paranasal Sinuses)

text: A 30-year-old woman presents with a chronic headache, facial pain, and nasal congestion. Her physician orders a Water's view X-ray of the paranasal sinuses (PNS) to further investigate her symptoms. Which of the following best describes the findings that the Water's view X-ray primarily visualizes?

A 40-year-old man presents with forehead pain, especially when leaning forward, and a feeling of pressure between the eyes. To evaluate the paranasal sinuses, his physician orders a Caldwell view X-ray. Which of the following sinuses is best visualized in a Caldwell view X-ray of the paranasal sinuses (PNS)?

A 25-year-old woman presents with chronic nasal congestion and postnasal drip. She has a history of recurrent sinus infections. The ENT specialist decides to order a Rhese view X-ray of the paranasal sinuses (PNS) to evaluate her ethmoid sinuses. Which of the following best describes the utility of the Rhese view X-ray in this patient's assessment?

options.label: A
options.text: It is primarily used to visualize the maxillary sinuses

options.label: B
options.text: It provides optimal visualization of the frontal sinuses

options.label: C
options.text: It is the preferred view for evaluating the ethmoid sinuses

options.label: D
options.text: It gives the best view of the sphenoid sinuses

text: A 50-year-old male with a history of headaches and visual disturbances is referred for imaging of the paranasal sinuses. His physician orders a basal (submentovertical view X-ray) Which of the following sinuses is best evaluated with this imaging view?

A 16-year-old boy presents with fever, headache, and swelling around his left eye. He has a history of chronic rhinosinusitis. On examination, he exhibits proptosis, ophthalmoplegia, and reduced visual acuity in the affected eye. A CT scan of the sinuses shows ethmoid sinusitis and evidence of an orbital abscess. Which of the following is the most likely complication of sinusitis in this patient?

A 58-year-old male presents with progressive dysphagia and occasional spitting of blood. Examination reveals no intraoral lesions, but a firm, bilateral upper deep cervical lymphadenopathy is present. Indirect laryngoscopy reveals a midline exophytic lesion over the posterior pharyngeal wall. What is the most likely diagnosis and best initial step for further evaluation?

options.label: A
options.text: Posterior pharyngeal wall carcinoma; proceed with endoscopy and biopsy

options.label: B
options.text: Postcricoid carcinoma; perform CT scan and barium swallow

options.label: C
options.text: Laryngeal carcinoma; schedule microlaryngoscopy for biopsy

options.label: D
options.text: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma; perform MRI of skull base and neck

text: A 42-year-old man presents with a 2-month history of unilateral nasal obstruction, serous otitis media, and a painless neck swelling. He also reports recent onset of facial pain and diplopia. Nasal endoscopy reveals a submucosal mass in the nasopharynx. Biopsy is planned. Which of the following investigations is most appropriate to assess both the extent of the primary tumor and skull base involvement before treatment planning?

options.label: B
options.text: Contrast-enhanced CT scan of the nasopharynx and neck

text: A 19-year-old male presents with mild dysphagia, posterior throat discomfort, and a gradually enlarging midline swelling on the posterior pharyngeal wall. He also has multiple cervical lymph nodes and a history of weight loss and low-grade fever. Cervical spine X-ray reveals destruction of C3 and C4 vertebral bodies. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.label: A
options.text: IV antibiotics and emergency incision and drainage

options.label: B
options.text: Incision and drainage followed by full antitubercular therapy

options.label: D
options.text: Immediate tracheostomy to prevent airway obstruction

text: Arrange the following antenatal investigations in sequential order: Triple markers test Nuchal Translucency Scan Growth scan Anomaly scan Select the correct answer using the code below:
Investigation of Choice for Vesico- Vaginal Fistula is:
Which of the following statements regarding the medical methods of termination of pregnancy is correct

options.label: A
options.text: It can be done only upto 72 days from LMP

options.label: B
options.text: There is no need for removal of copper T before initiating the management

options.label: C
options.text: Only a RMP registered for MTP can perform

text: Which of the following statements about partograph is false

options.label: A
options.text: Alert line starts at 4 cm cervical dilation

options.label: B
options.text: Action line starts 4 hrs after the alert line

options.text: Each of the small box represents 1 hr

text: Investigation of choice for vesicovaginal fistula is
The unicornuate uterus can be identified by which of the following investigations? Laparoscopy X-Ray Falloscopy HSG Select the correct answer from the given below code:
A Nursing assistant posted in obstetric care was asked to plot a Partograph to monitor the progress of labour

A 67-year-old female is brought to the OPD in a poor general condition. On examination, she was found to have a right ovarian mass. Her CT scan indicated peritoneal caking. Her CA-125 levels were 1200 IU/L. What would be the management in this case?
A 33 year old G2P1 at 18 wks was' found to be at high risk of NTD and low risk of trisomy 21 on quad test - what is the next investigation?
A 40-year-old woman visits gynaec OPD with h/o intermenstrual bleeding. This USG image shows a lesion within the endometrial cavity with a feeding vessel. What is the diagnosis?

A 25-year woman had evacuation of molar pregnancy done 6 months earlier. She now presents with general ill health, breathlessness, cough, and irregular vaginal bleeding. On chest X-Ray, there are canon ball metastases. Her beta hCG levels are persistently high. Which is the best management option?

options.label: A
options.text: Multi-dose Inj. Methotrexate and Inj. Folinic acid

text: A 20-year-old female presented with a webbed neck and shield chest. Which of the following findings are most likely to be seen in this patient?
A 28-year-old woman is undergoing evaluation for successive recurrent pregnancy losses. On ultrasound, a Mullerian anomaly is suspected. What is the best way to confirm this?
A 28-year P0A3 with recurrent 2nd-trimester abortions was found to have a midline uterine septum on sono-salpingography. What is the best management option?

The patient with normal menstrual cycles and now presents with delayed menses for 2 weeks with scanty vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain. Beta HCG is 1400 mIU/mL. Her blood pressure is normal. USG shows trilaminar appearance in the uterus and the adnexa is normal. What is the next step in management?

A woman at 26 weeks of gestation presents for routine evaluation. On examination, fundal height corresponds to 24 weeks. Ultrasonography revealed decreased amniotic fluid. Which of the following conditions would have led to this presentation?

Female with lower abdominal pain for one month, history of multiple sexual partners, mild intermenstrual bleeding, scanty vaginal discharge and dysuria which subsided on its own. The most likely causative organism is?
A woman undergoing infertility treatment is found to have bilateral tubal blockage on hysterosalpingography. What is the most appropriate next step in her management?

A 35-year-old man, involved in a motorbike accident, was initially unconscious but regained consciousness and seemed coherent upon arrival at the emergency department. After a few hours, he experiences a rapid decline in consciousness and develops a headache and right-sided weakness. A CT scan of the head shows extradural hematoma. What is this clinical presentation, characterized by a period of initial recovery followed by a rapid deterioration in consciousness, classically known as?

A forensic expert is reviewing a case involving the will of a deceased individual. The will was handwritten by the testator, a 55-year-old man who had been diagnosed with a progressive neurological disorder. It was written and signed in the presence of two witnesses a few weeks before the man's passing. The forensic expert is assessing the validity of the will based on legal standards. Considering the information provided, which of the following is most likely to affect the validity of this holograph will?

options.label: A
options.text: The will is valid as it was handwritten and witnessed.

options.label: B
options.text: The will is invalid if the testator was under undue influence.

options.label: C
options.text: The will is invalid as it was not certified by a legal authority.

options.label: D
options.text: The will is valid only if made during a lucid interval of mental illness.

text: At what age range would the initial ossification center of the pisiform bone most likely be visible on a wrist radiograph?

In a seminar, a discussion is centered around the early detection of pregnancy, a topic crucial in both clinical and forensic settings. The presenters focus on the utility of ultrasonography in pregnancy diagnosis. The participants are asked to identify the earliest period at which pregnancy can be diagnosed using ultrasonography.

In a case under investigation at a district hospital, a medical officer is required to estimate the gestational age of a fetus as part of a forensic examination. This is crucial in a legal case involving questions around the time of conception and fetal viability. The medical officer refers to ultrasound findings for accurate dating of the pregnancy. At the earliest, by which week of gestation can the gestational sac be seen using ultrasonography?

As a forensic resident, you are evaluating a case involving an individual who sustained multiple injuries under suspicious circumstances. Among the injuries, there is one that initially appears to be an incised wound but, upon closer examination, suggests a different mechanism of injury. Misconceptions about such wounds can lead to inaccurate conclusions. Which of the following statements about incised-looking lacerated wounds is NOT true?

options.label: C
options.text: Bleeding is more compared to incised wound

text: A forensic expert is reviewing a case where an adult individual was found deceased in a private residence with evidence suggesting an atypical context at the scene. The individual was discovered partially clothed with materials that constricted the neck and pornographic content in close proximity. There were no signs of forced entry or struggle, and the preliminary investigation indicated that the individual was alone at the time of death. The expert is tasked with determining the most likely behavior associated with the circumstances of death, given that there is a possibility of a sexual element to the asphyxiation. Which of the following behaviors is most commonly linked to the findings of sexual asphyxia in this context?

A 63-year-old male with a history of hypercholesterolemia and smoking presents to the emergency department with chest pain that started while he was mowing the lawn. The pain is described as a pressure sensation on his chest with radiation to his left arm. An ECG shows ST-segment elevations. Considering the most common location for myocardial infarctions, which area of the heart is most likely affected in this patient?

A 65-year-old man with a history of atrial fibrillation and hypertension was admitted to the hospital after being found unconscious at home. On examination, he was noted to have a focal neurological deficit. A CT scan of the head revealed an area consistent with an acute infarct. The patient deteriorated rapidly and was pronounced dead. At autopsy, the pathologist discovered a thrombus in the cerebral artery with a distinct coralline appearance. This finding is characteristic of which type of thrombus?

A middle-aged man from West Bengal presents to the clinic with complaints of numbness and tingling in his hands and feet, thickened patches of skin, distinctive lines across his nails, and "raindrop" pigmentation on his hands. These symptoms have progressively worsened over several months. Given the patient's geographic location and the constellation of symptoms, you suspect chronic exposure to a toxic substance. Which of the following toxins is most likely responsible for the patient's symptoms?

A medical officer at a district hospital is evaluating a housewife who accidentally ingested a white powder from a rodenticide. She presents with generalized flaccid paralysis, an irregular pulse, and her ECG shows multiple ventricular ectopics with generalized changes in the ST-T segments. Her serum potassium level is found to be 2.5 mEq/l. Based on these clinical findings, what is the most likely ingested poison?

A 32-year-old man is brought to the emergency room in an intoxicated state. He had consumed a significant amount of alcohol at a party. The medical team needs to estimate his blood alcohol level for medical and legal purposes. Which of the following methods is considered the most reliable for estimating blood alcohol level?
